Personnel & fronts Snap counts and FTN charting

Play-by-play personnel labels (11, 12, 21) aren't published for 2026. The nflverse participation file stops at 2025. These numbers are the closest public stand-in: the average number of players at each position per snap from snap counts, and FTN's per-play counts of backs, box defenders and pass rushers.

Play action from under center FTN charting, EPA from play-by-play

Play action is FTN's charted is_play_action flag on dropbacks (sacks and scrambles included). Under center is FTN's qb_location U. The comparison is every dropback without play action, from any alignment, because most under-center dropbacks are play action and the rest are too few to stand on their own.

Offense: how much, and does it help?

Under-center play action as a share of all dropbacks, against EPA per play on those plays minus EPA on dropbacks without play action. Above the line, play action is adding value. Dashed lines are league averages.

Other 31 teams

Defense: under-center play action faced

Share of opponent dropbacks that were under-center play action, against EPA allowed on them minus EPA allowed on other dropbacks. Axis flipped, so a defense that holds up better against play action sits higher.

Play action from shotgun FTN charting, EPA from play-by-play

Play action is FTN's charted is_play_action flag on dropbacks (sacks and scrambles included). Shotgun is FTN's qb_location S. The comparison is every dropback without play action, from any alignment, because most under-center dropbacks are play action and the rest are too few to stand on their own.

Heavy sets FTN backfield counts, EPA from play-by-play

Play-by-play personnel groupings (12, 13, 21, 22) aren't published for 2026, so heavy sets here means two or more players lined up in the backfield besides the quarterback (FTN's n_offense_backfield of 2 or more: a fullback, a second running back or an H-back), or an extra offensive lineman reported as eligible (jumbo, from the play description). Extra tight ends set on the line with a single back don't count, because nothing per play marks them. Teams' heavy rates track their average backs on the field from snap counts closely, not their tight ends. The comparison is every other pass and run play.

Offense: how often, and does it work?

Share of pass and run plays from a heavy set, against EPA per play from heavy sets minus EPA on all other plays. Above the line, the offense is better in heavy sets. Dashed lines are league averages.

Other 31 teams

Defense: heavy sets faced

Share of opponent plays from a heavy set, against EPA allowed on them minus EPA allowed on other plays. Axis flipped, so a defense that holds up better against heavy sets sits higher.

Who owns the sacks? Coverage sacks vs. protection losses

Pressure rate vs. pressure-to-sack rate

QBs with 40+ PFR dropbacks, plus the selected team's passers with 15+. Right means pressured more often, which points at the line. Up means more of that pressure became sacks, which points at the QB. Dashed lines are league rates.

QBsOther QBs

How each sack happened

Every sack sorted into one bucket using FTN charting, in this order: QB fault flag, QB out of pocket (extended play), blitz, otherwise the standard rush won.

"Extended play" sacks are the closest thing to coverage sacks: the QB left the pocket looking for someone open. "Standard rush won" means four or fewer rushers got home with the QB in the pocket, which usually means lost blocks, though a long hold can contribute.

Passer rating allowed by position group

Every target PFR charted against the defense. Lower is better; league average for all defenders is . Targets in parentheses. Yards here are PFR's charted coverage yards, which can run above a team's official passing yards allowed because PFR credits yards from its own charting.

Coverage by position group

Target share is the group's share of the team's charted targets. "Lg" columns are the league-wide figures for the same group. Snap reports list most edge rushers as LB, so a linebacker with 3+ pressures and at least twice as many pressures as targets counts as Edge.

Sources & method

  • Data as of Oct 14, 2026, covering regular-season Weeks 1–5 for all 32 teams (CAR and KC, on bye in Week 5, have four games). Pro Football Reference advanced stats (pressures, coverage, yards before contact, broken tackles) include Week 5 except Monday night's BUF–LA game, which PFR had not charted yet.
  • Section summaries are hand-written analysis where a team has it; otherwise they are generated from that team's numbers and state ranks and splits.
  • NFL Next Gen Stats (CPOE, time to throw, aggressiveness, rush yards over expected, separation, YAC over expected) via the nflverse NGS release, sourced from nextgenstats.nfl.com. NGS only publishes season figures for players above a volume cutoff, and we couldn't find the cutoff documented anywhere (the nflreadr documentation says only that NGS covers players "above a minimum number of pass/rush/rec attempts"). What the season data shows: In-game top speeds aren't available from this source.
  • EPA and success rate from nflverse play-by-play (nflfastR expected-points model). EPA per play uses pass and run plays; pass plays include sacks, scrambles count as dropbacks.
  • Play action, blitz, drops, interception-worthy throws from FTN Data charting, distributed by nflverse (files, field definitions).
  • Pressures, coverage, yards before contact, broken tackles from Pro Football Reference advanced stats, which usually land a few days after the games; snap counts from PFR via nflverse. Box score stats from nflverse weekly player stats.
  • DVOA from FTN's Week 5 DVOA ratings (Aaron Schatz, Oct 13, 2026), transcribed by hand.
  • Penalties from nflverse play-by-play. Only accepted fouls count; declined and offsetting ones don't. Each foul is read from the play description, so a play with two accepted fouls counts both. The player flagged is matched to that week's roster by team and jersey number, and his roster position decides the section: tight ends sit with receivers, and defensive linemen and linebackers with the front seven. Any flag on a kick or punt play counts under special teams. Fouls the officials charged to the team with no player named (delay of game, illegal shift, too many men) are listed as team flags.
  • Presnap motion from FTN Data charting (the is_motion flag, any player moving before the snap), joined to nflverse play-by-play for EPA, yards and success rate. It covers the same pass and run plays as team efficiency; dropbacks include sacks and scrambles, runs are designed runs. Motion rate rank: 1st is most motion. EPA ranks: 1st is best (highest on offense, lowest allowed on defense).
  • Play action by alignment from FTN Data charting (is_play_action on dropbacks, with the quarterback's alignment from qb_location: U under center, S shotgun, P pistol; pistol is shown separately in the alignment table but not ranked, since it's rare), joined to nflverse play-by-play for EPA, yards and success rate. Rates are shares of all dropbacks; the baseline is every dropback without play action from any alignment.
  • Heavy sets are a proxy, because play-level personnel isn't published for 2026: a play counts as heavy when FTN charts two or more players in the backfield besides the quarterback (n_offense_backfield), or when an extra offensive lineman reports as eligible (play description). It catches fullback, two-back, H-back and jumbo looks, not extra tight ends on the line with one back. Checked against snap counts: team heavy rates correlate 0.79 with average running backs and fullbacks on the field and −0.12 with tight ends.
  • Personnel is estimated. Average players per snap come from PFR snap counts; teams label edge rushers as DE, OLB or LB inconsistently, so DL and LB are combined into one front group. Backfield, box and pass-rusher counts come from FTN charting.
  • Sack attribution is an estimate. Pressure-to-sack rate uses PFR pressures and sacks; the buckets use FTN's per-sack flags. The time of each sack isn't public.
  • Ranks are out of 32 teams unless noted; 1st is best. Samples are four or five games, so treat every rate here as early.
